before: ‘Cursed is anyone who has sex with his father’s wife, for he has uncovered his father’s covering.’ All the people are to say, ‘Amen!’
after: ‘Cursed is anyone who has sex with his father’s wife, for he has uncovered his father’s garment.’ All the people are to say, ‘Amen!’
rationale: Uses garment for the same uncovering-the-father’s-kanaph expression already retained in public 22:30. This makes the recurring sexual-marital image recognizable without removing it or changing the prohibited relationship.
tsw_comparator: ‘Cursed is the one who lies with his father’s wife, because he has uncovered his father’s skirt.’ And all the people shall say, ‘Amen.’

before: He made him ride the heights of the earth and eat the produce of the fields. He let him suck honey from rock and oil from flinty stone.
after: The LORD made Jacob ride the heights of the earth, and Jacob ate the produce of the fields. The LORD let him suck honey from rock and oil from flinty stone.
rationale: Separates the Hebrew causative made-him-ride from the following finite he-ate clause. Naming the LORD and Jacob, already identified in 32:9–12, makes the two agents audible while preserving the rock/honey/oil images and poetic lineation.
tsw_comparator: He made him ride upon the heights of the land, and he ate the produce of the field. He made him suck honey from the rock and oil from the flinty rock,

before: Never again has a prophet like Moses arisen in Israel, whom the LORD knew face to face,
after: Since then, no prophet has arisen in Israel like Moses, whom the LORD knew face to face.
rationale: Keeps the narrator’s retrospective since and the LORD as the one who knew Moses. Ends a complete sentence before restating the comparison, so the relative clause cannot seem to modify Israel.
tsw_comparator: And there has not arisen a prophet since in Israel like Moses, whom the LORD knew face to face,

before: with all the signs and wonders the LORD sent him to perform in the land of Egypt against Pharaoh, all his servants, and all his land,
after: No prophet has matched him in all the signs and wonders the LORD sent him to perform in the land of Egypt against Pharaoh, all his servants, and all his land,
rationale: Restates the implicit comparison with a prophet like Moses as an English main clause. Preserves every recipient and the LORD’s commissioning, continuing the final comparison into verse 12.
tsw_comparator: none like him for all the signs and the wonders that the LORD sent him to do in the land of Egypt, to Pharaoh and to all his servants and to all his land,

before: and with all the mighty hand and all the great terror Moses displayed before the eyes of all Israel.
after: or in the mighty hand and all the great terror Moses displayed before the eyes of all Israel.
rationale: Completes the comparison begun in verse 11 and removes the awkward all-the-mighty-hand construction. The hand image, great terror, named Moses, and all-Israel witnesses remain intact.
tsw_comparator: and for all the mighty hand and all the great fear that Moses did in the sight of all Israel.
